context: The order of the vertex list V determines the matrix row and column indices. The headers give both the index and the vertex label. A 1 in M[i,j] means V[i] and V[j] are connected. A 0 means there is no edge.
description: An undirected edge joins two vertices. Adding or removing it requires updating both symmetric entries, M[i,j] and M[j,i]. Each frame's table shows the entire matrix after the operation.

To add a vertex, append a row and a column of zeros. To remove a vertex, delete its entire row and column. The matrix indices of later vertices decrease, but the vertices keep their identities and labels.

frames.announcement: Initially, V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with indices 0 through 4, a 5×5 matrix, and six edges. Both M[0,2] and M[2,0] are 0 because edge 1–2 is absent.
frames.explanation: Initially, V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4] corresponds to indices 0 through 4 in a 5×5 matrix. The six undirected edges are 1–3, 1–5, 2–3, 2–5, 2–4, and 4–5. Each contributes a symmetric pair of ones. Edge 1–2 is absent.
frames.key_state: Initially, V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4], with indices 0 through 4, a 5×5 matrix, and six edges. Both M[0,2] and M[2,0] are 0 because edge 1–2 is absent.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix, step 1: complete initial state

frames.title: Initialize the five-vertex graph

frames.announcement: Vertices 1 and 2 have indices 0 and 2. Add edge 1–2 by changing M[0,2] and M[2,0] from 0 to 1. All other entries stay the same. The matrix is still 5×5, and the graph now has seven edges.
frames.explanation: Vertices 1 and 2 have indices 0 and 2. Add edge 1–2 by changing M[0,2] and M[2,0] from 0 to 1. All other entries stay the same. The matrix is still 5×5, and the graph now has seven edges.
frames.key_state: After adding 1–2, V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4]. The matrix is 5×5, the graph has seven edges, and both M[0,2] and M[2,0] are 1.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix, step 2: complete state after adding edge 1–2

frames.title: Add edge 1–2

frames.announcement: Vertices 1 and 3 have indices 0 and 1. Remove edge 1–3 by changing M[0,1] and M[1,0] from 1 to 0. All other entries stay the same. The matrix is still 5×5, and six edges remain, including 1–2.
frames.explanation: Vertices 1 and 3 have indices 0 and 1. Remove edge 1–3 by changing M[0,1] and M[1,0] from 1 to 0. All other entries stay the same. The matrix is still 5×5, and six edges remain, including 1–2.
frames.key_state: After removing 1–3, V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4]. The matrix is 5×5, with six edges. Both M[0,1] and M[1,0] are 0, and edge 1–2 remains.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix, step 3: complete state after removing edge 1–3

frames.title: Remove edge 1–3

frames.announcement: Append isolated vertex 6 to V, giving V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6]. Its index is 5. The matrix grows to 6×6, with zeros throughout the new row and column. The other entries stay the same, and the graph still has six edges.
frames.explanation: Append isolated vertex 6 to V, giving V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6]. Its index is 5. The matrix grows to 6×6, with zeros throughout the new row and column. The other entries stay the same, and the graph still has six edges.
frames.key_state: After adding isolated vertex 6, V=[1, 3, 2, 5, 4, 6]. The matrix is 6×6, with six edges. The row and column at index 5, for vertex 6, contain only zeros.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix, step 4: complete state after adding isolated vertex 6

frames.title: Add isolated vertex 6

frames.announcement: Remove the row and column at the original index 1 for vertex 3, along with edge 2–3. V=[1, 2, 5, 4, 6], and the matrix shrinks to 5×5, with five edges. Vertex 2 keeps its label and moves to index 1. Vertex 6 remains isolated.
frames.explanation: Remove the entire row and column for vertex 3 (formerly index 1), along with its only remaining incident edge, 2–3. Edge 1–3 was removed in step 3. V becomes [1, 2, 5, 4, 6], at indices 0 through 4. The matrix shrinks to 5×5, with five edges. The indices of vertices 2, 5, 4, and 6 each decrease by one, but their labels stay the same. For example, vertex 2 moves from index 2 to index 1. Vertex 6 is now at index 4. Its row and column contain only zeros, so it remains isolated.
frames.key_state: After removing vertex 3, V=[1, 2, 5, 4, 6], at indices 0 through 4. The matrix is 5×5, with five edges. Vertex 2 keeps its identity at index 1. Vertex 6 is at index 4, with zeros throughout its row and column.

state_tables.caption: Adjacency matrix, step 5: complete state after removing vertex 3

frames.title: Remove vertex 3

summary: An adjacency matrix illustrates the difference between updating individual entries for edges and adding or removing whole rows and columns for vertices.
title: Adding and removing edges and vertices in an adjacency matrix
